modified_caption: The bar charts illustrate the accuracy percentages for different methods on the PHEME and PolitiFact datasets. Each chart contains six bars representing the categories: 'Ours,' 'w/o comments,' 'w/o text,' 'w/o select,' 'w/o emotion,' and 'w/o cognition,' placed along the horizontal axis. The vertical axis, labeled 'Accuracy (%),' uses a linear scale ranging from 75% to 95% with tick intervals of 2.5%. In the PHEME chart, the 'Ours' method achieves the highest accuracy at approximately 89.84%, followed closely by 'w/o select' at 89.80%. The 'w/o text' method shows a significant decline, reaching only 75.10%, the lowest value in the dataset. In the PolitiFact chart, the 'Ours' method again demonstrates the highest accuracy at 90.57%, while 'w/o comments' and 'w/o cognition' exhibit similar performance at 85.85% and 85.74%, respectively. The results suggest that removing text features has the most detrimental impact on accuracy, while the exclusion of comments and cognition leads to comparable performance levels across both datasets.

modifications.claim: 'w/o select' achieves an accuracy of 89.80% in the PHEME dataset.
modifications.reality: 'w/o select' achieves an accuracy of 88.80%, not 89.80%. The modified caption falsely inflates the value.

modifications.claim: 'w/o text' shows a significant decline, reaching only 75.10% in the PHEME dataset.
modifications.reality: 'w/o text' achieves an accuracy of 80.10%, not 75.10%. The modified caption falsely deflates the value.

modifications.claim: 'w/o comments' and 'w/o cognition' exhibit similar performance at 85.85% and 85.74% in the PolitiFact dataset.
modifications.reality: 'w/o comments' achieves 85.85%, but 'w/o cognition' achieves 87.74%, not 85.74%. The modified caption falsely swaps the value of 'w/o cognition' to make it appear closer to 'w/o comments.'
